a friend saw this game and instently showed me. i have a weakness for food games, and with a twist of goblins? i was sold literally the day before release. this game was not in my wishlist for 24 hrs before i bought it the next day.
its an easy game to learn but each run feels new as you unlock different meals and drinks. the runs can be quick and fast paced and its a perfect game for me to just zone out, kill time, and enjoy when i dont really know what i want to do

First things first, I HIGHLY recommend learning it like a typing game with full keyboard layout vs manually clicking everything - the sushi has rhythm. Key combos are way faster, trust me.
If you're a fan of the Cook, Serve, Delicious franchise, this hits that sweet spot but with the roguelike ability to add/remove/level up recipes to maximize $$$ during the 10 rounds of customers/landlord. Also reminiscent of a lot of cooking/time management games from the Flash era which I love!  

NYUM NYUM NYUM

You have NO IDEA how many HOURS I spent playing the Sushi-Go-Round flash game as a kid. This concept is incredibly similar but instead of unlocking the same recipes at each level, you unlock a random assortment of recipes via roguelite shop mechanics, plus price/efficiency modifiers. I have been waiting for a game like this for so long since flash died. I am going to make SO MUCH SUSHI.

Goblin Sushi scratched that itch that balatro triggered in me too. The runs and unlockables are fun and have a good length, and the gameplay is varied enough to keep you coming back for more. I'm really excited about the new restaurant locations and updates that will come over time. Good job, Team Old Cake Factory!

At first I thought this was just okay, my starter runs weren't great and I didn't really understand why I wasn't making enough money and failing out after day 3 or 4. Once I realized that the conveyer belt just constantly cycles sushi you've already made, the game turned into spamming key-combos for recipes, and it picked up pace exponentially. So I started focusing on one recipe that was easy to make and just optimized that as much as I could, so that I could make a ton of money really quickly spamming QE. Then they force gave me more recipes to learn because I ran out of rerolls for upgrades and the only upgrades left were for me to learn more key combos. Now I'm just spamming QE QED QEED QQDD QQRR and space while constantly clicking on the rice maker to get as much rice as possible, refilling sushi ingredients, and clearing plates that are left over. My landlord keeps harassing me for more and more money, and finally some large orc man brought his kids in and ate all of the sushi that I had on my conveyer belt so I'm spamming even more key combos now and... oh it's over.

This game might be good guys.

Edit - Game needs balancing unfortunately. There's a card called "Omakase!" that makes the game incredibly easy, breaking all requirements to meet demands from customers. So you can just pump out one simple two key recipe over and over again and exponentially improve that recipe with other cards. Apart from that, it's cute, it's fun, handmade art all that. I've been playing this game since the demo was out and genuinely love it. I like the art style and the sound design keeps you in it and relaxed while providing a real challenge. It's become my "just one more time" game since the runs are typically 20 minutes or so.

Great relax game, worthy for the price.
It has quite the replay value, each run is different (depending on randomized bonuses/cards you get on particular dishes) and I appreciate it makes you plan & think ahead. 

Quite fun coming up with new strategies like "how can I only serve poop to customers in this run and still make money" (yeah it works :D ).

My 3 biggest wishes for it now are:
- possibility to change Keybinds
- tweak some of the cards bit better. Lot of cards prefer Rice cooker to be running nonstop but the benefit of cards  buffing the opposite are quite low. More cards with cummulative buffs would be welcome i.e. for each dish without rice get X permanently and loose X if you make it with rice etc.
- show a weekly/monthly refreshed leaderboard (and keep the "all time") so there is higher motivation/end goal for me.

The game is great, but Twitch viewers ruin everything by spamming the same dishes over and over. I’d like to see more meta‑progression between runs, more automation, clear in‑game achievements, and greater build variety.
I really don’t understand the absurd numbers in the achievements — how is anyone supposed to play 500 runs?

I am absolutely in love with games that do roguelites but with unique new takes and this is just another one of them. I was enjoying Dogpile a lot this year (a roguelite x merging game with dogs) and My Card is Better than Your Card (roguelite but stickers and cards) and this just gives me the same vibes, where you just want to keep doing the next run over and over again.
Didn't encounter any bugs other than when a customer orders a recipe you removed from the game, the customer doesn't change what they ordered. 
Will keep playing and can't wait to see what the devs decide to add with the early access.

This game is extremely fun!!! I have absolutely been addicted to it ever since I've started playing. I even bought it on my ipad for when I'm away from the PC and bored ahaha. It's very reminiscent of old flash games that are cooking management games. Made me think of games like Cake Mania, Cook Serve Delicious, Spongebob Krusty Cook-off, and such. Great to know they'll have more updates and seems to have more places/locations in the game based on the menu. I'm excited for its future updates!

This is honestly a very charming game with a lot of personality! Lots of very funny visual gags with the clients, ingredients and the Landlord. The gameplay is fun and addictive, and it can be very fast-paced and challenging. I'm a big fan of management games and roguelikes so this is very much up my alley, and the 2D art style and overall look is lovely.

I do find myself kind of wanting something more from this game though, but I'm not sure what it is. Maybe once there is more locations and variety added it can truly become something I'd want to keep coming back to. But I do think what Early Access offers right now is not bad at all and is a solid game. Maybe a story mode would be cool??
I was also waiting to see what the price tag will be once the game is actually out as I received a Steam Key early, and I do think it's worth the current price with the features that are already added. You can easily get hours of fun out of this game, and I think it was a great idea to put it on mobile as well.
I will definitely be checking out future updates and I do wish the devs a lot of success as I believe it's a very small team and their first published game. Thanks a lot for letting me try it out!

Reminds me of the classic time management games but with the fun random aspects of a roguelite. Addicting and easy to get lost in and not so challenging that it feels impossible. I'm definitely looking forward to future updates!

2026 is shaping up to be another strong year for indie games, Goblin Sushi has the potential to be blow up (and I really hope it does) with it's addictive and satisfying gameplay. It hits that same strategic nerve as Balatro and Plate Up but with a gnarlier coat of paint, can't say I've ever put caterpillars in a sushi roll before this. Dirty customers with rambunctious children, smiling poop platters adorning the conveyer belt when you mess up a recipe (trust me, you will do this more than you might think). There is something strangely relatable about these mute goblin customers - save for their grunts of displeasure and murmurs of delight when slinging a fire roll out, even if admitting that makes me sound like I belong in Mount Massive Asylum. The pressure of paying rent on time while serving impatient goblins brings back my PTSD from working the Sunday church lunch rush at IHOP in my youth, this time with more fun and less anxiety.

Once you find a game-breaking strategy, it is easy to fall into a flow state where the inflationary rent stops being a threat. The developers clearly have a lot of passion for this project and it shows in the quirky details and beautiful art style. Each customer looks like they were made with intention, recipes have unique twists to them, the music is surprisingly catchy, the little things were done with more thought and care than most big budget titles these days. I don't think you can really put a price on the attention to detail and passion

Goblin Sushi:
~~~~~~~~~~ 

Did you know that Sushi was a high-end restaurant experience in America back in the 1960s? Believe it or not, a special Sushi roll back then cost around $3 to $5, which is equivalent to $30 to $50 in today's money. I can't recall having ever seen a Japanese restaurant when I was growing up in Geneva in the 70s or 80s. My first Sushi experience was around the mid-2000s, a whopping ten years after I touched down in the land Down Under. And let me tell you, I could stuff my face with Sushi like there was no tomorrow at my local Sushi train for $50 those days. But the boom of Japanese cuisine has grown so much that even imaginary beings are craving it! It's the turn of the Goblin world to be flooded with slices of raw fish on top of beds of rice. And you, my friend, you are the chef who will make it happen, in Goblin Sushi!    

Goblin Sushi is a casual cooking job simulator with roguelike and deck-building elements, developed by Old Cake Factory and published by Metaroot on the 10th of February 2026 on the Steam platform. At the time I am writing this review, the game is in early access, and the gameplay and content might change when it reaches version 1.0.

Really fun game with a satisfying progression curve. Worth the price if you're the kind of person who likes exploring various builds and combos in roguelite games. Some builds are ridiculously overpowered compared to others which can be a downside or make for a fun challenge depending on how you look at it. Overall I would still like the game to be a bit more balanced. 
Otherwise the art is neat, the music is alright and the story (if you can call it that) adds a layer of humour without being intrusive. 

The only real issue I have with this game is the lack of option to rebind keyboard shortcuts.

The new level has been a pleasant surprise. I expected minor differences but overall similar recipes and combos, and clearly underestimated the devs. It's different enough that I had to spend a couple runs finding my footing playing the hardest difficulty mode. 

If the devs keep adding levels without raising the price or shipping them as dlc, I'll probably consider buying the supporter pack.
